title: ADR-0018 — Bind prepublication evidence to tree content, not commit identity
description: Compare prepublication evidence against the git tree hash of candidate content, and run ci:prepublish as a real pre-merge required check, so the gate can be satisfied by a real merge.
searchText: adr-0018 — bind prepublication evidence to tree content, not commit identity compare prepublication evidence against the git tree hash of candidate content, and run ci:prepublish as a real pre-merge required check, so the gate can be satisfied by a real merge. decisions adr approved cicd security phase-1-5 prepublication evidence is now compared by git tree content, not commit sha identity, resolving 2026 08 10. context the completion audit's authoritative prepublication check gate compares prepublication evidence (produced by npm run ci:prepublish ) against the exact commit sha of the candidate under review, via validatepublicationcandidate 's hard fail check that evidence.candidatesha === candidatesha . that equality can never survive a real merge into main . github always server generates a new commit sha when a pull request is merged — whether by merge commit, squash, or rebase — even when the merged file content is byte identical to the reviewed branch tip. so evidence generated pre merge, bound to the pre merge commit sha, is structurally guaranteed to fail comparison against the post merge main head sha, regardless of how sound the underlying gates were. the gate was unsatisfiable by design, not by a bug in any individual gate. compounding this, evidence/publication readiness.json and evidence/publication evidence.json are local only, gitignored artifacts. ci:prepublish had never run as a required pre merge ci check, so even setting aside the sha equality problem, no ci produced evidence for a candidate existed to compare against in the first place. decision drivers the gate must be satisfiable by a normal, real github merge into main , not only by an artificial same sha condition that a merge can never produce; the gate must not become materially weaker in what it guarantees — it must still catch a case where the actual reviewed file content differs from what is being published; the fix should reuse an existing, precedented pattern in this codebase rather than invent a new content binding mechanism; evidence must actually be produced pre merge, by ci, not only by a local developer run, or the comparison has nothing authoritative to compare against. options considered this was an explicit decision made by the repository owner after investigation, not an autonomous engineering call. 1. rejected — relax the check to "candidate sha is an ancestor of the merged commit." this materially weakens the guarantee: it would also pass for a merge that manually resolved a conflict by hand editing content differently from what was reviewed, because a manually resolved merge commit has the reviewed commit as an ancestor regardless of what edits were made during conflict resolution. an ancestor relationship proves lineage, not that the published content matches what was evaluated. rejected because it does not survive the exact failure mode it would need to catch. 2. adopted, in combination — add a real, required ci check that runs ci:prepublish on the pull request itself, pre merge, uploading the evidence as a build artifact. this produces authoritative, ci generated evidence to compare against, rather than relying on a locally generated file that was never ci verified. implemented in this decision as .github/workflows/pr prepublish.yml , job id prepublish . 3. adopted, in combination — compare the git tree hash of the candidate's file content instead of the commit sha. a git tree object id is a content hash of the full file tree; two commits with identical tree hashes have byte identical file content regardless of their distinct commit identities (author, timestamp, parent, message). this is strictly not weaker than commit sha equality for the purpose this gate serves (detecting content drift between what was evaluated and what is published) — it is exactly the same equality class (exact match), just applied to content instead of to unrelated to content commit metadata. this was empirically confirmed against this repository's own merge history: commit 1658a4a (the current main merge commit) and its pr branch tip parent 4905825 have identical tree 18ab7e93c923e309444d9aa69533c1437a317c52 , confirming that a real, zero drift merge in this repository does produce identical tree content across distinct commit shas — the exact case this gate needs to tolerate. this option is also precedented by the diffsha256 content binding pattern already used in src/modules/orchestration/publication/publication policy.ts , which compares diff content hashes rather than commit identity for a related purpose. decision adopt options 2 and 3 in combination. reject option 1. publicationreadinessevidenceschema gains a candidatetree field (same 40 hex char shape as candidatesha , produced by git rev parse head^{tree} ). validatepublicationcandidate now takes (input, candidatesha, candidatetree) and hard fails when evidence.candidatetree !== candidatetree , rather than when evidence.candidatesha !== candidatesha . candidatesha remains in the schema and in the failure reason message for traceability, but it is no longer the field being compared for equality. scripts/ci/prepublish.mjs computes and records candidatetree alongside candidatesha when generating evidence. scripts/ci/authorize publication.mjs and scripts/agents/audit phase 1.5.mjs both resolve the candidate's tree hash and pass it through to validatepublicationcandidate . a new workflow, .github/workflows/pr prepublish.yml , runs npm run ci:prepublish base origin/main on every pull request targeting main and uploads evidence/publication readiness.json and evidence/publication evidence.json as a build artifact, so ci — not only a local developer run — produces authoritative, checkable prepublication evidence for a candidate before merge. implementation status this decision covers code, tests, the new workflow, and documentation only. the following is explicit follow up work, not done in this change: adding the prepublish job's check context to the main branch protection ruleset's required status checks ; enabling strict required status checks policy ("require branches to be up to date before merging") for that ruleset. both require a live github api mutation against the repository's ruleset, which is out of scope for this change and gated on a separate, later approval (see risks below). positive consequences authoritative prepublication check becomes satisfiable by a real github merge, closing a structurally unsatisfiable gate without weakening what it detects; prepublication evidence is now produced by ci on the pull request itself, not only by an uncommitted local file, giving the gate something authoritative to compare against; the fix reuses this repository's existing content hash binding pattern ( diffsha256 in publication policy.ts ) rather than introducing a new mechanism; the rejected "ancestor of" relaxation is explicitly documented as rejected, so it is not silently reintroduced later. negative consequences one more required field ( candidatetree ) must be kept in sync everywhere candidatesha is computed; the new pr prepublish.yml workflow adds ci runtime cost to every qualifying pull request; until the ruleset is updated (follow up work below), prepublish running in ci does not yet block a merge — it currently only produces evidence, it does not yet gate it at the github level. risks residual risk this change does not yet close: tree hash comparison against a pull request's own head can false pass content that has silently drifted from main , or false fail on unrelated main drift, unless github's strict required status checks policy ("require branches up to date before merging") is also enabled for the ruleset that requires the prepublish context. that live ruleset mutation is explicitly out of scope for this change and requires a separate live test then approval step: open a throwaway pull request, cause real drift on main , confirm the new prepublish check fails on a stale tree, sync the branch, confirm it then passes — only after that live verification should the ruleset be flipped via a gh api mutation, and only with separate approval. a tree hash comparison, like a sha comparison, only detects file content drift; it cannot detect a compromised ci runner producing an evidence file for content it did not actually evaluate — this remains an assumed trust boundary of the existing evidence model, unchanged by this decision. follow up work 1. open a throwaway pull request, cause real main drift while it is open, and confirm the new prepublish check fails against the stale candidate tree. 2. sync that pull request's branch and confirm prepublish then passes. 3. only after that live verification, and with separate approval, mutate the branch protection ruleset: add prepublish to required status checks and set strict required status checks policy to true . 4. re run npm run phase15:audit once the ruleset changes land, to confirm the agent platform required check style gate treatment extends correctly to prepublish . supersedes or superseded by new decision; superseded by: none. it amends the prepublication evidence mechanism introduced under adr 0017's platform completion scope without superseding adr 0017's overall phase boundary. source references
